cryptohome: Add key_name_for_spkac As part of a feature to side-load machine keys verified by remote attestation into the system-wide token using the enterprise.platformKeys.challengeMachineKey API, the SignEnterpriseChallenge method needs another argument that specifies the key name used for SignedPublicKeyAndChallenge. This CL adds a temporary method to crypthohomed dbus server that allows calling SignEnterpriseChallenge with a new argument, |key_name_for_spkac|. The browser will be updated in a follow up CL to use this method. DD: go/chromeos-va-registering-device-wide-keys-support BUG=b:35580115,chromium:988367 TEST=unit test: AttestationTest.EMKChallengeDifferentKeyForSPKAC Change-Id: I390ddfcc8b5197578d0b869c79f65ba9478f7436 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1714595 Tested-by: Andreea-Elena Costinas <acostinas@google.com> Commit-Ready: Pavol Marko <pmarko@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Leo Lai <cylai@google.com>

attestation: Add key_name_for_spkac This CL changes the SignEntepriseChallenge method so that a different key than the one used to sign the challenge request can be used for SignedPublicKeyAndChallenge. The purpose is to have a machine key verified by remote attestation that can be side-loaded into the system-token. DD: go/chromeos-va-registering-device-wide-keys-support BUG=b:35580115,chromium:988367 TEST=unit test: AttestationServiceEnterpriseTest.SignEnterpriseChallengeUseKeyForSPKAC Change-Id: Ic6cb3e9bcc2be9d53425942c60fce5267231ef12 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1714597 Tested-by: Pavol Marko <pmarko@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Pavol Marko <pmarko@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Pavol Marko <pmarko@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Leo Lai <cylai@google.com>

cryptohome: Stop binding TPM 1.2 delegate to PCR0 There are some Chromebook models with buggy firmware that sometimes changes the PCR0 value to an unexpected value. Therefore disable the binding for now for everyone, until those buggy models reach EOL - otherwise the Chrome OS attestation and smart card login features will be broken when the PCR0 is wrong. This CL is, effectively, a revert of https://crrev.com/c/1065826, which introduced the PCR0 binding.
